name: El Niño / La Niña
summary: Very strong El Niño: Oceanic Niño Index +2.46°C for Aug–Oct, still rising
state: NOAA's Oceanic Niño Index for August–October, the latest available on 10 Nov, was +2.46°C, far above the +1.5°C threshold for a strong event (NOAA CPC). The index rose from +1.80°C for June–August and +2.16°C for July–September, and has risen in every three-month period since early 2026.
for_you: A very strong El Niño tends to bring drought to southern Africa, Australia and parts of Asia, and heavy rain to parts of the Americas, over the coming months. National met services publish seasonal outlooks.

sources.title: NOAA Climate Prediction Center — Oceanic Niño Index (ONI)

why: ENSO reshapes global weather for a year at a time — droughts, floods, hurricanes and crop yields.
drivers: Pacific trade winds and ocean heat content.
